questions.q: What can you search and inspect on the Review Journal Entries page?
options: Only the total count of transactions for a ledger
Subledger journal entries by ledger, subledger application, event class, date range, or batch, including header and line-level detail
Only supplier master data
Only payroll records
questions.explain: The Review Journal Entries page lets a user search and open subledger journal entries with full header and line detail.

questions.q: What information is visible on an individual line of a reviewed subledger journal entry?
options: Only the total entry amount, with no line-level detail
The account, the debit or credit amount, the description built by the description rule, and any supporting references
Only the supplier's phone number
Nothing; lines cannot be viewed, only headers
questions.explain: Each line shows the account, amount, nature (debit/credit), the generated description, and any supporting references attached.

questions.q: What does "drilling from GL back to the subledger" mean, as described in this lesson?
options: Deleting a GL journal entry permanently
Starting from a General Ledger journal entry and tracing it back through the subledger journal entry to the original source transaction
Creating a brand-new journal entry from scratch in the General Ledger
Exporting GL data to a spreadsheet
questions.explain: Drilling back lets a user trace a GL journal to the subledger entry and ultimately to the originating transaction, such as an invoice or receipt.

questions.q: Why is drilling back through Subledger Accounting often necessary to answer "why does this GL account have this balance"?
options: Because the GL journal entry alone usually doesn't show enough transaction-level detail to answer that question
Because GL journal entries never contain any useful information at all
Because drilling back is purely optional and never actually needed
Because the General Ledger does not store any journal entries
questions.explain: The specific transaction-level answer to such questions is usually only visible once you drill back through the subledger entry to its source transaction.

questions.q: Why does this lesson recommend reviewing subledger journal entries routinely, not only when troubleshooting a known problem?
options: Routine review has no real benefit over reactive review
Reviewing routinely, especially after a rule change, catches mistakes early and cheaply, before many periods of transactions use a flawed rule
Routine review is required by law in every jurisdiction
Routine review automatically fixes any errors it finds
questions.explain: Catching a flawed rule early through routine review is far cheaper than discovering a systemic error after it has affected many periods of postings.
